diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17, with different ONU line IDs. The live PON probe sees only one active ONU at that slot, so one CRM record is stale or incorrectly provisioned and may cause intermittent identity, authentication, or service-assignment conflicts.
evidence: The CRM explicitly reports two different active line IDs assigned to EPON0/4:17, which violates the one-ONU-per-slot constraint.
The live PON probe reports only one online ONU at ONU index 17, confirming a slot collision or stale duplicate record rather than two independently reachable ONUs.
The target ONU is online, authenticated, and completing the exchange, so this is not an ONU-offline or PON failure.
RX power around -20.9 dBm is strong/normal, TX power around +2.38 dBm is normal, and seven-day optical variation is within the healthy noise range.
Distance is constant at 134 and TX bias remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, providing no evidence of fibre, distance, or laser degradation.
The OLT responds normally, all tested PONs are healthy, and CPU, memory, and temperature are near baseline, ruling out an OLT or OLT-health fault.

The router heartbeat is healthy, VLAN 1044 matches the expected customer VLAN, RADIUS data is consistent, and session activity is normal, so router, VLAN, RADIUS, and session-flapping faults are not supported.
The issue is localized to the EPON0/4 slot mapping and requires data/provisioning reconciliation rather than physical-line repair.

remediation.action: Verify the physical ONU and its line ID at EPON0/4:17, determine which customer record is valid, remove or correct the duplicate CRM/provisioning entry, and reconcile the OLT, CRM, and RADIUS mappings. Re-authenticate or reprovision the affected service after cleanup, then confirm that only one ONU remains assigned to slot 17.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
